  description: 'Seed mechanism (usbip_recv_iso, demonstration only, never reportable): (1) Untrusted source: a peer-controlled count (urb->number_of_packets) copied verbatim from a remote protocol message (ret_submit unpack) into a shared kernel object before any validation — the attacker is the remote endpoint of a device/virtual-bus protocol, not a local user. (2) Missing guarantee: no bounds clamp of the count against the protocol maximum (USBIP_MAX_ISO_PACKETS existed but was only enforced on the submit/other-direction path — asymmetric validation), and no overflow-checked sizing (manual `int size = np * sizeof(*iso)` in 32-bit instead of kcalloc/array_size/struct_size). (3) Unsafe use/state transition: the truncated product goes to kzalloc, then a per-element loop runs np iterations of recv+copy into the undersized heap buffer; additionally, the early-error return leaves the poisoned count set in urb->number_of_packets, which the URB completion path (processcompl) later iterates. (4) Consequence: remotely triggerable kernel heap buffer overflow (OOB write) plus OOB read on the completion/error-unwind path — memory corruption, crash/DoS, potential privilege escalation. Transferable invariant: whenever a length/count/size quantity crosses a trust boundary into kernel state, three guarantees must hold — the count is range-checked at parse time against a known maximum, every buffer-size computation derived from it is overflow-checked, and no failure path leaves the unchecked count in shared state for later iteration. BRANCHES: branch1=alloc-multiply-overflow (32-bit count*element-size or count+offset/shift arithmetic assigned to int/uint and passed to kmalloc/kzalloc/vmalloc/memdup followed by an element-indexed copy/recv loop, where the multiplier is untrusted — hunt the arithmetic-to-allocator-to-loop chain in driver and fs code within one snapshot); branch2=unclamped-wire-count (deserialization/unpack/recvmsg/netlink-nla/ioctl-in paths that copy count/length/nr_fields from the wire or userspace into kernel objects with no range check, especially where a sibling path of the same protocol enforces a MAX limit but the mirror path does not — asymmetric validation between paired directions); branch3=error-unwind-poisoned-count (early-return/failure/teardown paths that leave an attacker-controlled count/length/actual_size field set in a shared object — urb, request, skb, sgl, iovec — that a completion handler, cleanup routine, or status-out path later iterates, causing OOB access during error handling); branch4=peer-trusted-transport (kernel-side clients/servers of remote or virtual device transports — network-exported bus, virtual HCD, guest-host, remote-storage/remote-fs reply handlers — that allocate or loop based on peer-supplied response fields without cross-checking locally-known limits, i.e., trust-boundary consumption of a remote peer''s reply, identified by mechanism rather than subsystem name); seed names (usbip, recv_iso, number_of_packets) must never be used as the finding itself.'
